summary: Vector shape / compatibility issue causing sudden rerank ordering regressions after embedding model swap
description: Customer reports that after switching their embedding model from open-embed-v2-512 -> open-embed-v3-384 in their Dedicated pool, reranker results for several search flows degraded: top-N ordering changed unpredictably and relevance dropped. Some rerank requests return quickly but with low-quality ordering; others show higher latency and occasional 500s. Customer switched models to save cost and saw immediate impact in production traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In customer account (Acme Payments) with dedicated pool in eu-west, change embedding model to open-embed-v3-384 and leave reranker pinned to open-rerank-512. 2) Run batch of 1000 search+rerank calls against route /v1/rerank using stored corpus. 3) Compare top-5 ordering and relevance metrics to baseline (embeddings=512). 4) Observe increased mismatches and occasional 500 errors with traces pointing to reranker-service.
observed_behavior:
- Top-N ordering degraded for 12% of queries by manual eval sets.
- Some requests have 500 errors with stack traces referencing 'vector_dot_product: length mismatch'.
- Median tail latency for rerank increased from 110ms -> 420ms for affected route.
- Customer sees billing unchanged but perceived quality regression.
expected_behavior:
- Backwards-compatible behavior where swapping to a different embedding model should either be blocked if dimensionality incompatible with pinned reranker, or auto-converted/handled without quality regressions.
- No 500s due to vector length mismatches.
- Latency should not spike by >2x for same traffic pattern.

[2026-03-10T09:12:23Z] reranker-service ERROR vector_dot_product: length mismatch: expected=512 got=384 request_id=cf7a2b
[2026-03-10T09:12:23Z] api-gateway WARN response 500 for /v1/rerank request_id=cf7a2b
[2026-03-10T09:12:24Z] embeddings-service INFO batch_embed completed model=open-embed-v3-384 batch_id=b-91
[2026-03-10T09:15:05Z] serving-runtime WARN fallback_to_cpu due to incompatible kernel for seq_len=1024
investigation_notes: Initial triage: traces show the reranker operator assumes 512-d vectors and performs native dot-product kernel on GPU. When 384-d vectors arrive, there is an internal validation error in native kernel that surfaces as 500. We also observed a compatibility shim in Dedicated cluster that attempts to pad/truncate vectors on the CPU for 'compatibility' and that path is single-threaded causing latency spikes. Hypotheses: 1) Model metadata for open-embed-v3-384 didn't register dimensionality with routing layer so reranker was not alerted. 2) Compatibility conversion code path is causing both quality degradation (zero padding changes vector semantics) and latency due to CPU-bound conversions. 3) Some edge requests bypass the shim and hit GPU kernel causing length-mismatch 500s.

resolution: Workaround: instructed customer to pin embeddings to previous 512-d model (open-embed-v2-512) for their critical routes. Hotfix: deployed a reject-on-mismatch policy at the api-gateway/reranker entrypoint to return 400 with explicit error if embedding dimensionality != reranker expectation. Long-term: engineering to remove CPU-based padding shim and add explicit auto-conversion service that runs as a parallel GPU-accelerated batch reindex job. Follow-ups: create a console warning when configuring embedding/reranker pairings, add model-metadata propagation observability and retries, and offer migration reindex as a supported service for Dedicated customers.
